title: The Search for the Wicked Witch, part 6
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: Now the charm began to work. The sky was darkened, and a low rumbling sound was heard in the air. There was a rushing of many wings, a great chattering and laughing, and the sun came out of the dark sky to show the Wicked Witch surrounded by a crowd of monkeys, each with a pair of immense and powerful wings on his shoulders.
One, much bigger than the others, seemed to be their leader. He flew close to the Witch and said, “You have called us for the third and last time. What do you command?”
“Go to the strangers who are within my land and destroy them all except the Lion,” said the Wicked Witch. “Bring that beast to me, for I have a mind to harness him like a horse, and make him work.”
“Your commands shall be obeyed,” said the leader. Then, with a great deal of chattering and noise, the Winged Monkeys flew away to the place where Dorothy and her friends were walking.

Some of the Monkeys seized the Tin Woodman and carried him through the air until they were over a country thickly covered with sharp rocks. Here they dropped the poor Woodman, who fell a great distance to the rocks, where he lay so battered and dented that he could neither move nor groan.

Others of the Monkeys caught the Scarecrow, and with their long fingers pulled all of the straw out of his clothes and head. They made his hat and boots and clothes into a small bundle and threw it into the top branches of a tall tree.

The remaining Monkeys threw pieces of stout rope around the Lion and wound many coils about his body and head and legs, until he was unable to bite or scratch or struggle in any way. Then they lifted him up and flew away with him to the Witch’s castle, where he was placed in a small yard with a high iron fence around it, so that he could not escape.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the leader of the Monkeys say?
options: That she had called them for the third and last time
That they would not obey a wicked witch
That the Cap no longer had any power
That they had never been called before

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Witch order done with the Lion?
options: Brought to her, to be harnessed like a horse
Killed along with all of the others
Driven back towards the Emerald City
Left asleep among the daisies and grass

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where was the Tin Woodman dropped?
options: Over a country thickly covered with sharp rocks
Into the deep river that runs below the castle
In the middle of a field of scarlet poppies
At the gate of the Emerald City itself

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Monkeys do with the Scarecrow's clothes?
options: Bundled them into the branches of a tall tree
Burned them on the sharp rocks below
Carried them back to the Witch's castle
Left them lying on the grass where he fell

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where was the Lion put?
options: In a small yard with a high iron fence
In the great kitchen of the castle
In a cage with bars of gold
On the flat roof of the castle

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the sky do when the charm worked?
options: Darkened, with a low rumbling in the air
Cleared to a bright and cloudless blue
Turned green as it does in the city
Filled with smoke from the castle

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why could the Tin Woodman neither move nor groan?
options: He was battered and dented by the fall
The Monkeys had tied his jaws shut
His joints had rusted in the rain
He had been emptied of his straw

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why could the Lion not fight back?
options: He was wound round with many coils of stout rope
He had been struck senseless by the fall
The Monkeys were far too many for him
He was too frightened to move at all

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does immense describe?
options: The great size of the monkeys' wings
The noise the monkeys made
The height they flew above the ground
The number of monkeys called

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: The last call of the Cap scatters and destroys the party
The Winged Monkeys refuse the Witch's cruellest order
The Monkeys carry the whole party safely to the castle
The Witch changes her mind and spares the travellers

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how was the leader of the Monkeys marked out?
options: He was much bigger than the others
He alone had no wings
He wore the Golden Cap himself
He spoke in a woman's voice

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Monkeys pull out of the Scarecrow?
options: All the straw from his clothes and head
The pole that held him upright
The paint from his painted eyes
The basket he was carrying

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what sound came with the Monkeys?
options: A rushing of wings, chattering and laughing
A silence so deep it frightened them
A roaring like a great fire
The ringing of many small bells

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Witch want the Lion alive?
options: To harness him and make him draw her about
To set him to guard her castle gate
To trade him to the Winkies for work
To frighten the Emerald City with him

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the Monkeys do the moment they had their orders?
options: Flew straight to where the travellers were walking
Argued with the Witch about the girl
Waited until nightfall to attack
Asked to be released from the charm

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does stout describe about the rope?
options: Thick and strong
Short and frayed
Wet and slippery
Woven out of straw

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: Three companions are broken, scattered, and caged in a single attack
The Monkeys carry the party to the Emerald City
The Witch's last charm fails to reach the travellers
The Lion fights the Monkeys and drives them off
